messages:
maria: heads-up — i'm sketching a 'permissions policy proxy' concept in the console/control plane. goal: centralize per-request routing/quota decisions and surface them to the Console so SDKs and clients stay thin.

jon: quick Q: isn't that duplicating routing policy infra we already have? extra hop sounds risky.

maria: not a heavy data-plane hop — think control-plane shim that annotates requests with decision headers for the runtime. runtime still enforces. proxy handles policy evaluation, canary flags, and simulated decisions for UX.

sanjay: main concern is cache churn and telemetry volume. where do we store counters and how often do we push them?

emily: from product POV we need the console to show "effective permissions" and "quota impacts" per-route. having the proxy emit trace IDs would help map policy decisions -> dashboard.

jon: alternative: bake more into scoped tokens (claims for routing/quota). That avoids another service but requires token-minting changes across SDKs and more rollout pain.

maria: correct. proxy acts as a migration shim: older clients get policy headers, newer clients can carry richer tokens.

kevin: suggestion: signed header approach to keep things auditable and tamper-evident. example header:
```
X-RW-Policy: v1 role=tenant-admin;scope=routes:read;quota=1000;rid=abc123;exp=1766549000;sig=BASE64SIG
```

sanjay: signed header fine, but replay protection is required. include nonce + short expiry. also TTL on decisions so runtime cache doesn't thrash.

emily: product feature ask: simulated mode where console shows what would happen without enforcement (customers can preview). need toggle per-tenant and per-route.

maria: yes — plan is: sim mode + canary by tenant. simulated decisions get a tag 'policy:simulated' so analytics/alerts can filter them.

jon: telemetry: we need both aggregated counters (for dashboards) and sampled detailed decision logs (for audits). retention: counters 90d, decision logs 7d by default. agree?

kevin: counters emitted by proxy asynchronously to our ingestion pipeline. enforcement remains in runtime. batching config: flush every 2s or when batch size > 500 — prototype needed.

sanjay: for Dedicated/Private customers the proxy must be optional or deployable in-customer VPC. some customers won't allow control-plane network egress.

emily: also enterprise requirement: audit events for role/scope changes must flow into the same audit pipeline. proxy should emit structured audit events with actor, before/after, and tenant.

maria: migration path idea: 1) implement proxy in staging with sim-mode only; 2) add header format + signing; 3) enable canary enforcement for opt-in tenants; 4) iterate on SDK token-minting to move claims later.

jon: I'll draft SDK impacts and a deprecation timeline for token-claimless clients.

sanjay: i'll prototype counter batching + TTL heuristics this week and report numbers.

kevin: i'll sketch signing scheme and replay nonce flow; also an example verification snippet for runtime.

emily: product will mock console widgets: simulated decisions timeline, per-route quota burn graph, and policy audit trail.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/proxy-service v0.1 -> staging :rocket: (build 4589)

maria: great — i'll write a short RFC with header contract and sim API. please comment by EOD so we can sync on the API tomorrow. ping me here for blockers.
